candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes progressive gait disturbance, cognitive decline, and white matter hyperintensities, which are consistent with gliomatosis cerebri. While there is a mildly elevated CSF protein, there is no mention of ventriculomegaly or other features suggestive of Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus. The symptoms are better explained by diffuse white matter involvement.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus vs. gliomatosis cerebri
